paper.title: Cooperative Stochastic Multi-agent Multi-armed Bandits Robust to Adversarial Corruptions

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative stochastic multi-agent bandits with adversarial corruptions
unmapped: N (paper's V) agents play the same K-armed instance simultaneously; any pair may communicate, communication cost (bits) is also measured
corruption level C is summed over agents of sup-norm corruption and is a random variable; learner is agnostic to C
settings.definition_quote: Consider a set of $V$ agents ... interact with $K$ arms ... All rewards are assumed to be supported on $[0,1]$. ... The corruption level across all agents and rounds is measured as C= \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{v=1}^V \Vert r_v(t) - r_v^{S}(t) \Vert_{\infty}. The adversary is allowed to be adaptive ...

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative stochastic multi-agent bandits with adversarial corruptions (lower bound, two-armed instance)
unmapped: N (paper's V) agents play the same instance simultaneously with communication
settings.definition_quote: consider a two-armed bandit instance where $V$ agents interact with arm $1$ and arm $2$. The arm $1$ is with Bernoulli reward $\mu_1=1/2-\Delta$ and the arm $2$ is with a constant reward as $r_2=\mu_2=1/2$.

algorithms.name: Cooperative Bandit Algorithm Robust to Adversarial Corruptions (Algorithm 1)

source.label: theorem1
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg1} which is agnostic to the corruption level $C$, with probability $1-\delta$, incurs $O(K \log T)$ communication cost and regret as O(VC+\frac{ K \log T \log((VK\log T)/\delta) }{ \Delta_{\min}} ), and incurs the expected regret $\mathbb{E}[R_T]$ as O(V\mathbb{E}[C]+\frac{ K \log T \log(VT) }{ \Delta_{\min}} ).

results.notes: Paper's V (number of agents) mapped to N. Regret is pseudo-regret R_T (through means, summed over agents) bounded with prob 1-delta. Also O(K log T) communication. For V=1 gives O(C)+O~(K/Delta_min).

source.label: theorem1
source.quote: and incurs the expected regret $\mathbb{E}[R_T]$ as O(V\mathbb{E}[C]+\frac{ K \log T \log(VT) }{ \Delta_{\min}} ).

results.notes: Expected value of pseudo-regret R_T; obtained by setting delta=1/T.
Communication cost in bits (messages counted as O(K) per epoch, O(log T) epochs).

conditions: algorithm guarantees pseudo-regret O(log(VT)/Delta) in stochastic two-armed environments with Delta in (1/4,1/2) for sufficiently large T
corrupted instance with corruption level C = V T^alpha, alpha in (0,1)

source.label: theorem2
source.quote: For any $V \geq 1$, if a bandit algorithm with $V$ agent(s) that guarantees a pseudo-regret bound as $O(\log(VT)/\Delta )$ in stochastic environments with two arms and $|\mu_1-\mu_2|=\Delta \in (1/4,1/2)$ for sufficiently large $T$, then, there is an corrupted instance with corruption level $C=VT^\alpha$ ... such that with at least a constant probability $R'_T=\Omega (C-\sqrt{VT\log(VT)} )$. Then, $\mathbb{E}[R'_T]=\Omega (\mathbb{E}[C]-\sqrt{VT\log(VT)} )$ and $ \mathbb{E}[R_T]=\Omega ( \mathbb{E}[C] + \mathbb{E}[R'_T])$.

results.notes: R'_T is regret against best arm in hindsight on corrupted observed rewards (expected_regret). Also holds with constant probability for realized R'_T.

symbols.Rprime_exp: E[R'_T], expected regret w.r.t. corrupted observed rewards against best arm in hindsight

conditions: algorithm guarantees pseudo-regret O(log(VT)/Delta) in stochastic two-armed environments with Delta in (1/4,1/2) for sufficiently large T
corrupted instance with corruption level C = V T^alpha, alpha in (0,1)
results.notes: Shows additive E[C] unavoidable for expected pseudo-regret. Theorem 3 also gives E[R_T]=Theta(Rbar_T+E[C]) relations (not recorded).
